whatsHappening.background: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises, driven by years of armed conflict, repeated displacement, and weak access to basic services. Violence in the east, especially in North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri, has uprooted millions of people and worsened hunger, disease risk, and insecurity. Civilians are caught between armed groups, national forces, and a collapsing protection environment. The crisis is especially severe for children, women, and displaced families living in overcrowded sites or host communities with limited food, water, and health care.

civilianImpact.experiences: Civilians in Congo are living through repeated displacement, insecurity, and severe deprivation. Families fleeing violence often arrive in overcrowded camps or host communities with little shelter, food, or clean water. Children face interrupted schooling, trauma, malnutrition, and heightened risk of recruitment or abuse. Women and girls face especially serious risks of sexual violence and exploitation. In many areas, access to health care, sanitation, and protection services is extremely limited, making an already dangerous crisis even harder to survive.

image.alt: Displaced civilians in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

howToHelp.summary: The crisis in Congo receives far less attention than many other emergencies, even though the scale of need is enormous. Donations to trusted relief organizations can help fund food assistance, shelter, child protection, clean water, emergency health care, and support for displaced families. Public awareness matters too, because underfunded crises become even more deadly when the world stops paying attention.

civilianImpact.experiences: The civilian impact is not just about fleeing violence. People who escape attacks often end up in places where basic survival is still uncertain. Overcrowded sites can lack safe water, sanitation, and medical care. Children face rising malnutrition, missed schooling, and severe emotional trauma. Families lose livelihoods when fields, markets, and transport routes are cut off by insecurity. Even when aid reaches them, funding gaps mean many needs still go unmet, leaving people trapped between conflict and deprivation.

howToHelp.summary: Support for Congo helps keep people alive in one of the world’s most under-recognized emergencies. Funding can provide therapeutic food for malnourished children, emergency shelter, safe water, medical care, and protection services for families displaced by violence.

learnMore.text: Humanitarian groups in Congo are responding to hunger, displacement, disease risk, and protection threats, but they remain severely underfunded.

whatsHappening.background: Helping Congo means supporting civilians living through conflict, displacement, and hunger. Relief organizations are working to provide food aid, emergency shelter, nutrition treatment, safe water, health care, and child protection, but the needs are far greater than the available funding.

timeline.description: Support trusted groups already responding to hunger, displacement, and child risk.
Follow verified humanitarian reporting so Congo is not ignored.
Raise awareness about a crisis that remains major but underreported.

image.alt: Image representing humanitarian response in Congo

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping Congo does not require solving the entire conflict. It means supporting people who need food, protection, shelter, and medical care right now. Awareness also matters because the scale of Congo’s emergency is often overlooked, even as millions remain hungry and displaced. Donations and education can both help close that gap.

image.alt: Humanitarian support and civilian resilience in Congo

howToHelp.summary: Donate to trusted humanitarian organizations such as UNICEF, WFP, UNHCR, and coordinated emergency response groups working in Congo. Learn more from verified humanitarian reporting and keep attention on a crisis that remains severe, underfunded, and too often overlooked.

learnMore.text: Additional sources and organizations to follow include UNHCR and OCHA. Supporting food aid, protection, shelter, and child services can make a real difference.
